sections.name: Bed
styles: even energy from start to finish

annotations.intro: Point at the problem, and let a coding agent fix it.

clips.text: Hold Alt, click an element, and describe the change.
The Pi coding agent takes the annotation and edits your source.
The fix is on the page, without a full reload.

devtools.intro: Optional devtools put your stack's logs and controls inside the page.

clips.text: Hover the log minimap for real-time output from your services.
The Services panel lists every service, each with a restart control.
Browse your Git worktrees without leaving the page.
TanStack Query's own devtools open from the same toolbar.

docker-backed-services.intro: Give a Docker container a local HTTPS hostname. Docker still starts and stops it.

clips.text: This service is unmanaged: devhost routes to it but never starts it.
Docker starts the container.
Its port is published on the host's loopback address.
Start the stack.
devhost starts no process. It publishes the container's HTTPS address.
The container answers on its HTTPS hostname.
Stopping the stack removes the route.
The container is still running.
Removing it is Docker's job.

environment-variables.intro: devhost hands each service its port, its hostname, and your own variables.

clips.text: This service declares two variables of its own.
Start the stack.
devhost assigns a free port and starts the service.
The service received its port, bind host, hostname, and your message.
Stop the stack.

managed-caddy.intro: One proxy. Local HTTPS hostnames. Route each service by path.

clips.text: Two services share one hostname, split by path.
Start the stack.
devhost starts both and publishes an HTTPS address for each.
The hostname alone reaches the web service.
The API path reaches the API service.
One command stops both services.

managed-daemon-style-services.intro: devhost starts a background daemon, checks on it, and stops it.

clips.text: This daemon has three commands: start, status, and stop.
Start the stack.
devhost runs the start command and waits for the health check.
The daemon answers on its HTTPS hostname.
Stopping the stack runs the daemon's stop command.
The daemon is no longer running.

manifest-includes.intro: Each package owns its services. The root starts them together.

clips.text: The root manifest declares no services. It includes each package's manifest.
Each package declares its own service.
Start from the root.
devhost merges them into one stack.
The merged stack answers on its HTTPS hostname.
And it stops as one.

react-highlight.intro: Connect your Neovim cursor to the page running in your browser.

clips.text: Start Neovim with the devhost launcher. Here, it runs off screen.
Move the Neovim cursor to the heading. The page highlights it.
Move the cursor again, and the highlight follows.
Images work too. Source maps match the JSX to the page.
Leave the JSX, and the highlight clears.

service-references.intro: Point one service at another, even when its port is assigned at start.

clips.text: The API address is a reference, not a fixed port.
Start the stack.
devhost fills in the API's port and starts the API first.
The web service called the API at the resolved address.
One command stops both services.

shared-managed-caddy-settings.intro: Your stacks share one Caddy. Turn on plain HTTP and choose its ports.

clips.text: The shared Caddy settings turn on plain HTTP and set both ports.
Start the stack.
The HTTPS address now uses the port you set.
The service answers over HTTPS.
The same service answers over plain HTTP.
Stop the stack.

stack-lifecycle.intro: Start dependencies first. Stop the whole stack with one command.

clips.text: The web service depends on the API.
Start the stack.
devhost starts the API first, then the web service.
The web service answers on its HTTPS hostname.
Stopping takes one command.

troubleshooting.intro: Save a broken manifest and the running stack stays up. Fix it, save again.

clips.text: A stack with one service.
Start the stack.
The service is running.
Now save an invalid port.
devhost rejects the reload and says why.
The running stack still answers.
Save a corrected manifest.
This time the reload is applied.
The service shows the new configuration.
Stop the stack.
